Check a Project Against Overleaf's Limits

Source: R/rProject-size-check.R
SizeCheck.Rd

Measures what goes to Overleaf: every file in the project except local-only folders (.git, .verify, .library, .Rproj.user, detritus) and build output that make writes and Overleaf never gets (docs, pkgdown, quarto, .setup/build, .setup/latex/pdf, .setup/quarto/bib), the local-only data tiers (.setup/data-external, .setup/data-cache), and images (.sif).

Usage

SizeCheck(
  path,
  editable = 7,
  text_file = 2,
  file = 50,
  total = 100,
  files = 2000L,
  error = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Character string. Project path.

editable

Numeric. Limit for all editable text, in MB.

text_file

Numeric. Limit for one editable text file, in MB.

file

Numeric. Limit for one file, in MB.

total

Numeric. Recommended limit for the whole project, in MB.

files

Integer. Limit for the number of files.

error

Logical. If TRUE, stop with an error when a check fails.

Value

Returns a data frame of checks with the columns check, status, and detail.

Details

  • Editable text (fails): non-binary files in total above editable MB. Overleaf's GitHub sync stops above 7 MB.

  • Text file size (fails): any non-binary file above text_file MB. Overleaf caps editable files at 2 MB.

  • File size (fails): any file above file MB. Overleaf caps uploads at 50 MB.

  • Number of files (fails): more than files files. Overleaf allows 2,000.

  • Total size (warning): above total MB. Overleaf recommends under 100 MB with GitHub sync or git.

  • Duplicates (warning): files of at least 1 MB with the same content.

The report also lists the largest text files and the largest files.
